summary: In an interview with FRANCE 24, Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe said the Trump administration had "an unbalanced approach" in implementing the DR Congo peace deal it brokered. He also said that the recent row over the Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie's top job was "manufactured in Paris and Kinshasa". Finally, he defended a deal for Rwanda to host failed asylum seekers from five European countries.

title: Nigeria: States set to get their own police forces
summary: Nigeria has moved a step closer to letting its 36 states set up their own police forces. The National Assembly has sent a constitutional amendment bill to the president, as authorities seek state-run police to complement the federal force amid growing insecurity. Many states currently fund vigilante groups to fight armed groups like Boko Haram, but these groups are poorly trained and ill-equipped for the task. FRANCE 24's correspondent has the latest.

title: Senegal: Pastef removes President Faye from its ranks
summary: In Senegal, Pastef, the majority party led by National Assembly president Ousmane Sonko, has made official the departure of President Bassirou Diomaye Faye. It is the latest episode in a split with his former Prime minister that was already largely complete, and it comes in the middle of an economic crisis.

title: President Bassirou Diomaye Faye excluded from Senegal's ruling party
summary: In tonight's edition: The political divorce between Senegal's president and his powerful former prime minister and mentor is official. Also, all of Nigeria's states have shown willingness for a push to create their own police forces. Plus we see how in parts of the continent, conflict and a drop in funding have placed huge pressure on children's learning.

title: Predictable: DR Congo-Rwanda rivalry spills over to Francophonie summit
summary: François Picard is pleased to welcome Phil Clark, professor of international politics at SOAS University of London. The diplomatic crisis between Rwanda and DR Congo spilling out at the Francophonie summit in Phnom Penh has exposed an unexpected shift in their relations. Clark says that "nobody expected Rwanda to back down in this way" following President Emmanuel Macron's request that President Paul Kagame withdraw Louise Mushikiwabo's candidacy for a third term as head of the group.

title: Rwanda to host hub for rejected EU migrants
summary: In tonight's edition: Five European countries are negotiating a deal to deport rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda. Also, DR Congo and Rwanda's political animosity spills over at the Francophonie Summit in Cambodia. Plus in Tunisia, young women are increasingly turning towards weightlifting and bodybuilding as a form of self-expression.

title: Canaries urge government action after 2,200 migrants reach the islands in 48h
summary: Spain says nearly 2,200 migrants have arrived by boat to the Canary Islands this weekend. The Spanish islands are one of the main entry points into Europe for migrants from Africa. The Spanish Interior Ministry says more than 13,000 arrived there between January and the end of last month. Details and analysis by Andrew Hilliar, FRANCE 24 international affairs editor.

title: A deep dive into Ivory Coast's solar energy goals
summary: Can Ivory Coast, which remains heavily dependent on fossil fuels, turn to solar power to make its energy consumption greener and more sustainable? We visited the country's new solar power plant in Ferkessédougou, in the north of the country. Inaugurated in July, it is expected to generate nearly 90 gigawatt-hours of electricity a year. Report by Julia Guggenheim.

title: Cape Verde's President José Maria Neves wins second term
summary: Cape Verde's President Jose Maria Neves won re-election on Sunday with 63.8 percent of votes cast, provisional electoral commission results showed. Neves had been the favourite in the West African archipelago. His main challenger was Joana Rosa Amado, the country's first woman presidential candidate, who conceded and congratulated Neves Monday morning.

title: Guinea opens illegal gold mining trial, 1,200 people arrested
summary: Guinea opened a trial over illegal gold mining on Thursday, November 12, after a crackdown on mineral extraction in the district of Siguiri. There was a ban on "unregulated and illegal" gold mining in the area where the military was subsequently deployed. Security forces have expelled tens of thousands of foreign nationals who had come to work in the region's mines.

title: Toera's homecoming: Madagascar's slain king joins his ancestors after 129 years
summary: In 1897, French colonial troops killed King Toera, ruler of Madagascar's powerful Sakalava kingdom of Menabe, and took his skull to Paris, where it remained hidden in a museum for more than a century. France returned the remains last year, and for the first time since his death, King Toera took his place among his ancestors during the Sakalava people's most sacred ritual.

title: Amnesty criticises South Sudan, UN over failure to heed massacre warnings
summary: Amnesty International said Thursday, November 12, that South Sudan and UN peacekeepers failed to act on warnings of a massacre that ended with more than 200 dead in March. The world's youngest country has been plagued by civil war, poverty, corruption and intercommunal violence since it was formed in 2011. FRANCE 24 spoke to Donatella Rovera, Senior crisis response adviser at Amnesty International.

title: Across Africa: Tunisians drawn into Russia's war with Ukraine
summary: This week: A new report says more than 1,400 Africans have been recruited to fight for Russia in Ukraine since 2023. Also, as South Africa races to become Africa's digital gateway, a growing backlash is emerging in Cape Town. Plus music, dance and theatre lit up Abéché as the city's arts festival in Chad drew crowds of young spectators.

title: NGO criticises UN's response to massacre in South Sudan
summary: In tonight's edition: Amnesty International accuses both the government and UN peacekeepers of failing to protect civilians during a massacre in South Sudan that killed over 200 people. Also, more than a thousand people are prosecuted for illegal mining in Guinea. Plus a century after French colonial troops killed him, a Malagasy king has finally come home.

title: Violent clashes near the Sudanese border: At least 65 dead in western Ethiopia
summary: Tom Canetti, our correspondant in Ethiopia, has more.

title: French journalist Christophe Gleizes marks 500 days in Algerian jail
summary: Having been detained for 500 days in an Algerian prison on charges of “glorifying terrorism”, French journalist Christophe Gleizes continues to serve a seven-year sentence despite an intense campaign by his family and friends and the football world. While awaiting a presidential pardon, his supporters are stepping up their media campaign to secure his release. FRANCE 24 spoke with his friend Pierre de la Saussay.

title: Africa: Ghana waste dump poses health, environmental 'crisis'
summary: An acrid haze hung over a sprawling dump in Ghana's capital, Accra, as excavators gouged into mounds of smouldering rubbish. Thin plumes of black smoke curled from burning plastic and rubber, mingling with the rank odour of stagnant lagoon water.

title: 'Friends' But Who Benefits? Notes from an Historic Summit, Myanmar's Genocide Ruling, Time to 'Bre-join' the EU?
summary: Welcome to the World This Week with Gavin Lee. You give us 45 minutes, we'll give you 7 days worth of crystal clear analysis. As ever, alongside a handpicked panel of four distinguished foreign correspondents.

title: What impact will the Shenzhen summit have on the US-China trade war?
summary: Despite warm words between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at three-way talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen Thursday, the simmering trade war between Washington and Beijing still looks to be no closer to resolution.

title: Bangladesh: Hasina supporters vandalise ruling party office
summary: Hundreds of supporters of ousted Bangladesh premier Sheikh Hasina staged street protests on Thursday, as a wave of arson attacks escalated tensions ahead of her planned return from exile next month.

title: ICJ ruling on Myanmar genocide: ‘Historic victory for Rohingya, landmark for international justice’
summary: Erin Ogunkeye welcomes Reed Brody, Member of the International Commission of Jurists, Human Rights Lawyer and veteran war crimes prosecutor. The International Court of Justice's ruling on Myanmar marks, according to Brody, "a historic victory for the Rohingya, but also a landmark for international justice." He explains how the court assessed evidence of genocidal intent, rejecting Myanmar's justification of its military operations as counterterrorism. He argues that "the existence of an armed conflict or a security objective doesn't exclude genocidal intent," a finding he believes will have "f

title: Xi demonstrating China's 'global status', occupying 'central position' in relation to Trump & Putin
summary: Sharon Gaffney is pleased to welcome Rex Li, professor of international relations at King's College London. For Professor Li, the meeting between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin in China is less about "reaching concrete agreements and a common position." Rather, he argues, it is about demonstrating Xi's ability to bring the American and Russian leaders together to discuss major geopolitical issues. Li believes that Xi Jinping has the most to gain from the meeting, as it allows him to demonstrate China's global status and its role as a diplomatic convener. Putin may also benefit fro

title: ICJ rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
summary: In August 2017, after attacks by a Rohingya militia, Myanmar’s army launched a “clearance campaign” in Rakhine state, with survivors describing mass killings, rapes and burned villages as hundreds of thousands fled to Bangladesh. The Gambia took Myanmar to the ICJ in 2019, and after a seven-year legal fight the court has ruled that Myanmar committed acts of genocide. Meanwhile some 1.2 million Rohingya remain in crowded camps, unable to return home.

title: China summit ends with little new, Europe backs Ukraine in Berlin
summary: The leaders of China, the United States and Russia met in Shenzhen for a historic first, but the summit brought little new: non-binding statements on peace and no plan to meet regularly. In Berlin, Europeans gathered to show their support for Ukraine, a pointed answer to a summit where Europe had no seat, as FRANCE 24's Kethevane Gorjestani explains.

title: In South Korea, women forced into prostitution on US military bases seek justice
summary: Tens of thousands of women were forced to work in South Korean state-sanctioned brothels used by American soldiers based in the country after the Korean War. They were raped, physically abused and forcibly confined. Now, after decades of silence, some of these women are speaking out.

title: 'Their lives, their rights, their history': Not the end of accountability for the Rohingya people'
summary: Oliver Farry welcomes Sonya Sceats, Director and CEO of the British Institute of International and Comparative Law. The case brought by The Gambia against Myanmar before the ICJ, and the court ruling, both have great significance for the Rohingya people, the interpretation of the Genocide Convention and the possibility of future criminal proceedings. The case could also have important implications for South Africa's proceedings against Israel, where there are “many similarities between the two cases.”

title: What to know about Xi, Putin and Trump's historic trilateral summit
summary: China's Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin and his US counterpart Donald Trump met for a historic summit in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday, where they agreed on a "peace declaration". The three leaders pledged to reform the UN, increase supplies of refined petroleum products and uphold the immunity enjoyed by officials in international courts.

title: Myanmar's Rohingya case: how does the ICJ define genocide?
summary: The ICJ is preparing to rule on whether Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, in a case brought by The Gambia after the 2017 crackdown. The key legal test is proving intent to destroy a group, which is notoriously hard, and the court’s reading of it could also weigh on South Africa’s case against Israel.

title: 'We are making history,' says Trump at historic trilateral with Xi and Putin
summary: The first meeting in history between US, Chinese and Russian leaders has kicked off in Shenzhen, China. "We are really making history," said the US president to his counterparts.

title: APEC Summit: Lots of gloss, little real progress?
summary: Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin are holding their first-ever trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, on the sidelines of the APEC forum. It is a historic moment in more ways than one, with the leaders of the world’s three most powerful countries around the same table. Ukraine, the war in Iran, nuclear disarmament and artificial intelligence are all expected to be discussed, and the summit has stoked fears of a carve-up of the world into spheres of influence. But despite the buzz, analysts expect more symbolism than substance, with few concrete breakthroughs likely. Our correspondent in the

title: Xi, Trump, Putin: historic summit ends, outcome unclear
summary: The unprecedented trilateral summit between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin ended on Thursday in Shenzhen after about an hour and 20 minutes. No details have emerged yet, but the three leaders talking face to face is already an event. Each has their own agenda: Putin wants to be back on the world stage, Trump needs a win at home, and Xi is asserting China’s status as an economic superpower. What comes out of it remains unclear, as FRANCE 24's journalists explain.

title: APEC Summit: Trump, Putin, Xi hold 'historic' meeting
summary: 🇺🇸 🇨🇳 🇷🇺 US President Donald #Trump, Russia's Vladimir #Putin and Chinese leader #Xi Jinping kicked off their first trilateral talks in Shenzhen. Beijing said the meeting is aimed at "safeguarding world peace", but it has raised fears of a carve up of the globe into "spheres of influence".

title: Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin begin unprecedented summit in China
summary: Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin opened their first trilateral talks in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the APEC forum, a meeting analysts expect to offer more symbolism than breakthroughs and that critics fear could carve the world into spheres of influence. Ukraine, the Iran war, nuclear disarmament and AI are all expected to come up, while Trump and Xi also held one-on-one talks on trade and technology.

title: South Korea tightens security for national exam over AI cheating scandal
summary: More than 550,000 candidates sat South Korea’s Suneung university entrance exam under extraordinary security, after an AI cheating scandal in which a top scorer on a national tax accountant exam admitted using a hidden mini camera to send questions to an AI system. Authorities inspected students’ glasses, deployed thousands of extra supervisors and ordered stickers over every button on candidates’ clothing. A nationwide disaster alert was also sent to make even muted phones buzz, exposing any devices smuggled into exam rooms.

title: Nuclear arms at the center of the Shenzhen trilateral meeting
summary: Nuclear weapons are at the top of Donald Trump’s agenda at the trilateral summit in Beijing. The US president wants the United States, Russia and China to reduce their nuclear stockpiles, and FRANCE 24’s Philip Turle expects him to push hard for a three-way agreement on the issue. Iran is also a key part of the discussion. The three leaders share an interest in preventing the Iranian regime from acquiring nuclear weapons. Regional conflicts and oil prices are also se to be central issues.

title: APEC summit: AI and tech competition between US and China
summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping is welcoming US President Donald Trump and Russia’s Vladimir Putin on Thursday for the first-ever three-way summit between the leaders. Beyond the wars in Ukraine and Iran, artificial intelligence and emerging technologies are expected to feature in the talks between Washington and Beijing, as the two powers compete for the lead in AI, advanced chips and other strategic technologies.

title: Myanmar committed genocide against Muslim Rohingya minority, UN court finds
summary: The United Nations International Court of Justice on Thursday ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against its Muslim Rohingya minority. It is the ⁠first time a state ​has been ‌found responsible for genocide at the ‌court.

title: Trump, Xi and Putin agree a nuclear war 'must never be fought' at landmark meeting
summary: US President Donald Trump, China's Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed on Thursday at a historic trilateral summit in Shenzhen, China, that a "nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought". Read our blog to see how the three-way talks unfolded.

title: Xi welcomes Trump: Does Nvidia scandal upend US-China AI race?
summary: You can strike Jensen Huang from the guest list, but good luck steering dinner conversation away from the topic in Shenzhen. The co-founder of the AI computing giant was set to accompany the US president to the APEC summit before he was undone by revelations of a dalliance with a Chinese national that happened to coincide with a Singapore client's backdoor skirting of sanctions on its powerful H200 chips.

title: Trump, Xi, Putin summit: What was it all about?
summary: Donald Trump has left China after a historic first meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the APEC summit. Ukraine was discussed without Kyiv or European leaders in the room, which raised eyebrows, though Trump defended dialogue with rivals and Putin said the talks created conditions for future agreements. Xi warned major powers against conflict, and topics included reducing nuclear risks, reforming the UN and increasing energy flows.

title: Haiti: Salvador’s Bukele publishes video of attack on gang leader’s house
summary: Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele said Wednesday that his troops demolished the lavish home of a prominent gang leader in Haiti known as Jeff Gwo Lwa. "My gift to the Haitian people on the anniversary of the Battle of Vertières," Bukele wrote on X - referencing a 1803 battle critical in helping secure Haiti's independence from France.

title: US Democrats nominate Jeffries to be first Black House speaker
summary: Hakeem Jeffries is on the cusp of becoming the first Black speaker of the US House of Representatives after Democrats elected him their leader Wednesday following a sweeping midterm election triumph. Jeffries faced no declared challenger, although opposition from some newly elected progressives had exposed divisions over how Democrats should wield their newfound power. FRANCE 24's Fraser Jackson reports from Washington.

title: Hegseth makes surprise trip to Venezuela, renews military cooperation
summary: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth made an unannounced visit to Caracas on Wednesday, announcing a resumption of military cooperation with Venezuela and vowing to crack down on drug traffickers. The trip marks the highest-level US visit since the ouster of Nicolas Maduro in January, signalling a dramatic shift in relations between the two countries.

title: Trump says he takes possible Iran bomb threat to Washington 'very seriously'
summary: President Donald Trump said Tuesday that US authorities take any possible threats to Washington ‘very seriously’, following reports that Iran was planning to target senior Trump administration officials, possibly with a radioactive bomb. Tehran dismissed the reports as ‘fabricated’.

title: Chase outage disrupts US online banking, Zelle payments
summary: Users of several major US banking apps and online portals reported outages on Monday, according to the monitoring site Downdetector.com, with one institution ruling out a cyberattack as the cause. Among those affected by the outages were Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase and the popular money transfer app Zelle.

title: Trump says he needs funding for air traffic control after ground stop
summary: US ​President ​Donald Trump, pressed on a ​technology ‌failure ⁠that ‌grounded thousands of ⁠flights last week, ​on ‌Monday told reporters ‌that ​the government needed funding for upgrade ​to ​air traffic ​control equipment. FRANCE 24's Monte Francis speaks with Sheldon Jacobson, Professor of Computer Science at the University of Illinois. He explains that "the Republicans have had full control of the House and the Senate since the President came in. They controlled everything. If they needed the money and wanted the money they could have approved the money. The fact that they didn't, in the t

title: US judge strikes down Trump visa restrictions on foreign students, journalists
summary: A US federal judge struck down a Trump administration policy on Monday that would have sharply limited the length of time foreign students and journalists could stay in the country, ruling that the proposed restrictions were unlawful and would undermine educational opportunity.

title: November 17 blackout hoax: How a conspiracy theory went viral around the world
summary: A conspiracy theory claiming a worldwide "blackout" will hit the world on November 17 has spread across social media, with the claim it will cut electricity, internet and banking services. The rumour stems from a routine US FEMA emergency alert test, but was amplified by cryptocurrency accounts, misleading claims about EU preparedness advice and references to "The Simpsons". Recent technology outages, flight disruptions and cyberattacks have added to public anxiety, helping turn a routine test into a global hoax.

title: Pope concludes South America homecoming, reassures faithful after cancer scare
summary: Pope Leo XIV finished Monday his 12-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru reiterating his advocacy for social justice, environmental protection and the importance of community. Just a month after undergoing lung cancer surgery, the 71-year-old pontiff drew millions of faithful across South America, where he spent nearly two decades as a missionary.

title: The new faces of the US Congress
summary: The United States Congress is about to welcome dozens of new faces. A majority of them, Democratic, after the "blue wave" in the midterm elections. FRANCE 24's Washington correspondent Fraser Jackson catches up with one of these new lawmakers as they go through orientation as they prepare to take office in January. He speaks with Katy Padilla Stout, U.S. Representative-elect for Texas's 23rd congressional district.

title: 'Record number of women elected' to US Congress & governorships in midterm elections
summary: Following the 2026 US midterm elections, Gavin Lee welcomes Politico Senior National Politics Reporter Lauren Fedor to discuss the growing number of Democratic women elected to Congress and governorships, particularly mothers of young children.

title: Jensen Huang: The French Connection
summary: President Trump is heading to Asia in a few days' time, where he is due to meet President Putin and President Xi. But there could be one fewer tech giant at the table: Jensen Huang, who has resigned from Nvidia amid a suspected espionage affair.

title: US probes nationwide flights stoppage as travel disruptions persist
summary: US air travel is expected to return to normal this Sunday, following a nationwide ground stop Friday night that stranded hundreds of thousands of passengers and disrupted travel worldwide. The Trump administration blamed the incident on a botched replacement of old copper wire communication lines and said there was no evidence this was a cyberattack. The ground stop now raises questions about the country's aging infrastructure and lawmakers are calling for an investigation. Analysis by Philip Mann, aviation expert at Vector Strategic Consulting.

title: Air travel issues persist in the US after nationwide ground stop
summary: After almost five hours of grounded flights in the US, flights have resumed. However, passengers are still waiting and wading through tough logistics to get to their destinations after massive delays and cancelled flights. Details by Simon Moritz.

title: Skyscraper in Riyadh damaged as Saudi Arabia reports surge in new Houthi attacks
summary: A skyscraper in Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh was damaged on Thursday after the Gulf country reported new attacks by Yemen's Houthis. Witnesses said the city's Public Investment Fund Tower, which showcases Saudi Arabia's economic ambitions, was "damaged across several floors, with windows blown out".

title: Gaza: Israel launched new offensive on Nuseirat
summary: Israeli tanks have moved east of the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza, with witnesses reporting heavy shelling, gunfire and airstrikes as the Israeli military says it has launched an operation in a Hamas-controlled area. Strikes killed at least three people on Wednesday, and displaced families are fleeing again, saying there is no real ceasefire. Israel and Hamas accuse each other of breaking the truce in force since October 2025, while Gadi Eisenkot tries to form a government after inconclusive elections.

title: Middle East crisis poses 'largest threat' to energy security in history, warns IEA
summary: The International Energy Agency said on Thursday that the Middle East crisis triggered by US and Israeli strikes on Iran in February posed the “largest threat” to energy security in history. It warned that consumers were bearing more of the costs as Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz disrupted oil shipments.

title: Israeli army launches ground operation in Hamas-controlled area of Gaza
summary: The Israeli military said it had launched an operation on Wednesday in a Hamas-controlled area of central Gaza, where an AFP journalist saw Israeli tanks position themselves east of the Nuseirat refugee camp. The rare ground operation comes after inconclusive Israeli elections, with the opposition's Gadi Eisenkot trying to form a government without caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has built his brand on saying he will ensure Israel's security. FRANCE 24's Daniel Whittington reports.

title: Writer Etgar Keret: 'The Israel my parents dreamed of' is still possible, but not under Netanyahu
summary: François Picard is pleased to welcome Israeli writer and filmmaker Etgar Keret, author of "The Seven Good Years". Keret argues that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is seeking to remain in power, at any cost, including delegitimising Arab parties and prolonging conflict. "For him, it could be a never-ending war as long as he's in power. He has no incentive to stop it," our guest warns.

title: Did the US use ‘blackout bombs’ in Iran? Images reveal mysterious fibres at infrastructure sites
summary: Photographs published by Iranian local media suggest that US forces may have used graphite bombs, also known as ‘blackout bombs’, against infrastructure in Iran in recent days. These weapons are designed to disrupt electricity supplies by causing short circuits rather than physically destroying power facilities.

title: Yemen's Houthis advance on Aden as government forces retreat to defend their capital
summary: Houthi forces in Yemen have advanced to within 60 kilometres of Aden, the seat of the country's internationally recognised government, military and government sources said Sunday. The embattled government earlier announced it was pulling back its last forces from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to defend its temporary capital on the southern coast of Yemen.

title: Israel kills senior member of Hamas's military wing in Gaza strike
summary: The Israeli military said on Sunday its forces had killed a senior member of Hamas's military wing in Gaza. The militant group confirmed the death of Samir Abu Younis, the commander of its Rafah brigade, adding that he played a prominent role in planning the October 7, 2023 attacks.

title: Iran claims drone attack on US military base in Bahrain
summary: Bahrain issued two alerts of potential threats on Sunday, its first such warnings since September as blasts rocked the capital, Manama. It comes after Iran targeted an airbase in the US-allied island state, ending a long lull in strikes during the Middle East War and comes as negotiations to end the conflict remain at a stalemate, with the US maintaining its naval blockade and Iran its stranglehold over the strait of Hormuz. Story by Rachael Griffiths.

title: Bahrain says air defences destroyed several Iranian drones attacking US base
summary: Bahrain issued two alerts of potential threats on Sunday, its first such warnings since September. The second Iranian drone attack in three days, ending a long lull in strikes during the Middle East war. Diplomatic efforts to end the almost nine-month conflict have yet to produce a breakthrough, with ​sporadic attacks continuing. Details from the ground by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Tehran, Reza Sayah.

title: Global diesel prices ease as winter approaches
summary: Global diesel prices, which have remained elevated since the start of the Iran war and the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, have fallen sharply in recent weeks as Gulf exports recover and global oil supplies get back on track for the first time since February. The price drop is being felt in Europe, where prices remain roughly 77% above pre-war levels, and in the US, where the national average fell below $6 a gallon on Saturday. Details by Liza Kaminov.

title: Iran claims drone attack on US military airbase in Bahrain
summary: Iranian military confirmed on Sunday an attack on a US military base in Bahrain, in its second targeting the Middle Eastern country in the space of three days. Bahrain's military said it had intercepted several Iranian attacks, with the foreign ministry confirming its air defence systems had shot down Iranian drones, preventing them from reaching their intended targets.

title: Three sentenced to death over Jordan church attack
summary: A Jordanian court on Sunday sentenced the three gunmen responsible for a terror attack on a church funeral procession in the village of Hamoud that killed nine and wounded others. The attack prompted retaliatory strikes on "terrorist organisations" in neighbouring Syria.

title: Netanyahu renews call for Israeli unity government as Eisenkot dismisses 'tricks'
summary: Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday renewed his call for a national unity government with Gadi Eisenkot, who dismissed the appeal as a political ploy. This comes as the incoming premier is in the midst of negotiations to form a new administration.

title: West Bank: ‘Without international trade and financial support, large settlements would not exist’
summary: France is considering legislation to restrict trade with Israeli settlements in the occupied Palestinian territories, namely the West Bank. Ivar Ekeland, Professor Emeritus at Paris Dauphine-PSL University and Chair of the Organization of Academics for the Respect of International Law in Palestine, discusses the proposed measures with Alison Sargent. He calls for restrictions to cover n ot only goods but also services, including financial services, insurance and tourism. title: UN refugee chief Barham Salih slams 'shameful' war in Sudan, urges 'political solution'
summary: In an interview with FRANCE 24, UN refugee chief Barham Salih called the war in Sudan "shameful" and urged the world to end it. With forced displacement at a record high, he warned that funding cuts are hurting people "in dire need". "Efficiency has its limits," he said. Salih also defended the "integrity of the asylum system".

title: The truth about Douma: How Syria covered up a chemical attack
summary: On April 7, 2018, the Syrian town of Douma, on the outskirts of the capital Damascus, was targeted by a chemical attack. Evidence pointed to the Syrian regime, yet proof vanished, and eyewitnesses went silent. Eight years later, FRANCE 24's Jenna Le Bras tracked down survivors and witnesses of the deadly attack. She also met representatives of some of the world's most powerful institutions to understand how a massive cover-up campaign had been orchestrated by the regime, with Russian support.

title: 'No war, no peace' situation between US and Iran 'cannot continue', Iraqi FM says
summary: In an interview with FRANCE 24, Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said the "no war and no peace" situation in the region "cannot continue". He also said that closing all but two border crossings with Iran, as Washington demands, was "not possible". Finally, he confirmed that Iraqi oil now is now flowing through the Strait of Hormuz under US protection.

title: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills six, including surgeon, medics say
summary: Israeli fire killed 11 people in Gaza on Thursday, six of them in the bombing of Nasser hospital in south Gaza early in the day, health officials said, the deadliest single strike since Israel's elections last month. FRANCE 24's Mark Owen speaks with Dr Goher Rahbour, a surgeon working at the Nasser Hospital.
